prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP’s 2010 manifesto argues that only leaving the EU can deliver three essential freedoms: action (so Britain decides its own laws, trade and industrial support), resources (ending vast EU costs and red tape), and people (restoring democratic control to Westminster and voters). The party calls for a new referendum on EU membership, direct democracy, and a clean break from an unaccountable “EU superstate” that imposes law, undermines courts, and drains billions.

Economy and tax: Simplify and cut taxes to revive a productive economy. Raise the personal allowance to £11,500; introduce a 31% flat tax (merging income tax and employee NI), phase out employers’ NI (“tax on jobs”), and abolish Inheritance Tax when feasible. Replace EU VAT with a Local Sales Tax, return more business rates to councils, cut quangos and non-jobs to 1997 public-sector size, and scrap swathes of EU regulation. Restore the Bank of England’s authority, separate retail and investment banking, raise capital ratios, and curb risky credit expansion.

Jobs, enterprise, skills: Rebuild British manufacturing with long-term programmes in defence procurement, nuclear power, flood/coastal defences, transport and prisons—targeting one million skilled jobs. Create Production Enterprise Centres for SMEs. Denationalise universities/FE via student and training vouchers. Protect strategic firms by tightening takeover rules. Scrap costly EU carbon schemes.

Immigration and asylum: End mass immigration with a five‑year freeze; thereafter cap permanent immigration to around 50,000 on a strict points system. Leave the EU to regain border control; require visas/work permits, criminalise overstaying, triple border staff, deport illegal migrants, reject amnesties. Enforce first-safe-country asylum with secure centres; repeal the Human Rights Act, withdraw from the ECHR, and restore the Primary Purpose Rule. End state promotion of multiculturalism and reaffirm a single, tolerant British culture.

Law and order: Elected police boards; life means life; double prison places; three‑strikes for persistent offenders; stronger self‑defence rights; withdraw from the European Arrest Warrant; boot camps for young offenders; abolish the CPS.

Defence: Increase spending by 40%; expand the Army and TA; restore the Navy and carriers; strengthen the RAF; back NATO not EU forces; maintain/renew Trident; cut MoD bureaucracy; improve forces’ pay and care.

NHS and public services: Keep care free at point of use but slash waste. Elected County Health Boards; remove bureaucratic layers; franchise services to not‑for‑profits and private providers on fixed budgets; health credit vouchers for private cover; restore matrons and vocational training; free eye tests and dental check‑ups. In education, introduce school vouchers, retain/expand grammar and specialist schools, prioritise core skills and discipline, end social engineering, and restore grants via vouchers.

Pensions and welfare: Create a non‑means‑tested £130/week Citizen’s Pension; target tax relief at ordinary earners; freeze unsustainable public‑sector schemes; scrap PPF/NEST; simplify benefits into a Basic Cash Benefit that supports work, with enhanced child and nursery support limited to residents.

Foreign affairs and trade: Leave the EU for a Swiss‑style free trade deal; reclaim the UK’s WTO seat; champion a Commonwealth Free Trade Area; pursue global trade pacts; promote real human rights and self‑determination.

Energy and environment: Be sceptical of costly climate alarmism. Deliver 50% nuclear, support clean coal, end onshore wind expansion (offshore only if viable), repeal the Climate Change Act and EU energy diktats, and invest in flood defences and electrified transport while cutting green bureaucracy.

Transport, housing, constitution, culture, countryside and fishing: Invest in roads and three high‑speed rail lines; fair fuel duty; charge foreign HGVs; oppose Heathrow expansion in favour of a Thames Estuary hub. Control housing demand by controlling immigration; restore local planning via binding referenda; protect green belts. Introduce citizen‑triggered referenda, electoral reform (AV+), elected local boards, an English Parliament within Westminster days, recall of MPs, abolish regional quangos, and uphold the monarchy and national institutions. Promote civic nationalism, merit, British history and values; confront extremist Islam (ban burqa/niqab in public buildings, deport hate preachers, reaffirm UK law over sharia). Support British farming via WTO freedom, fair labelling, co‑ops, and a supermarket ombudsman. Leave the Common Fisheries Policy, reclaim a 200‑mile EEZ, end discards and industrial trawling, and rebuild the fleet. Protect animal welfare, Post Offices/Royal Mail, pubs (with smoking rooms), and SMEs.
